question: For $A=\begin{bmatrix}1&-1\\1&-1\end{bmatrix}$ and $B=\begin{bmatrix}1&k\\1&k\end{bmatrix}$, determine $k$ if $AB=O$.
explanation:
Step 1: Multiply the matrices using the row-by-column rule.
Step 2: We have $$AB=\begin{bmatrix}1&-1\\1&-1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1&k\\1&k\end{bmatrix}.$$
Step 3: The entries are $1(1)+(-1)(1)=0$ in the first column and $1(k)+(-1)(k)=0$ in the second column. The second row gives the same results.
Step 4: Thus, $$AB=\begin{bmatrix}0&0\\0&0\end{bmatrix}=O$$ for every value of $k$.
Step 5: Hence, there is no restriction on $k$; $AB=O$ for all real values of $k$. This demonstrates that non-zero matrices can have zero matrix as their product.
